**Three facts about lighthouses:**
1. The word "lighthouse" is derived from the ancient Greek name "Pharos," referring to the famous Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
2. Lighthouses often use Fresnel lenses, which were invented in the early 19th century to produce a beam of light that could be seen from great distances with less fuel and light loss.
3. Many historic lighthouses are now automated; the last resident lighthouse keeper in the United States, at Port Clyde Light in Maine, was replaced by automation in 1998.
